questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Going two a different cultural and academic environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, we had received a lot of information which made orientation easier, however the information was so extensive, and the steps to take after arrival so complicated, that it was still quite demanding to sort out. In addition, many things remained unclear specifically with respect to course registration, even after classes had begun, however the staff responsible for integrating exchange students were very helpful and easy to reach.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received many pamphlets of information and had persons of contact that would help us figure out things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Course information was difficult to get a hold of, and course registration was in particular very frustrating as agreed by almost all international exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared rooms (two people per room). Excellent condition, good facilities and great access to campus amenities. Overall very happy.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were dozens of excellent cafeterias on campus, with amazing and very varied dining options (although mainly chinese cuisine). As elsewhere in China, food and grocery delivery was cheap and convenient. The dormitory kitchen (shared) was simple, with only a microwave oven, a sizeable refrigerator, a sink and a water dispenser.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student housing and amenities are excellent, and seemed to be widely available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course registration was by far the most chaotic and frustrating part of the stay of exchange, as agreed by most international exchange students at Tsinghua.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course information was scarcely available in advance, and based entirely on previous courses offered, some of which were cancelled or unavailable. Since full-degree students get priority and prior access to the course registration system, many courses are furthermore fully booked before even being accessible for registration by exchange students. In addition, particular courses were not listed in the portal while no information as to why was provided, and required interested students to seek out departments and professors on our own initiative. From when the system opened to exchange-students, less than a week before start of classes, and a few weeks into classes, most if not all exchange students were still uncertain about their options.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Aside from information passed out in advance and during orientation, there was dedicated staff to answering questions and helping students with the procedures.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, I am very happy with the courses I was able to enroll in - they were all relevant to my academic interests and English-taught.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice students, to be prepared and accepting of the fact that there is a lot of uncertainty with regards to courses available on arrival; however, with a little persistence and patience, it should work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Excellent, challenging and interesting for the most part.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was quite different; often a lot less participation and dialogue with the class, compared to what I am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Quantum Field Theory (1), Machine Learning, Advanced Algorithms and Combinatorics, Analytical Mechanics, Elementary Chinese (B)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: In particular Quantum Field Theory (1) and Analytical Mechanics for those interested in physics. Advanced Algorithms and Combinatorics for students of computer science or with interests in cs, and mathematically minded.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots and lots of student-clubs and activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Student-clubs, travel, Beijing is a vibrant city with lots of culture and history.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Traveling, and befriending other Chinese students. Learn Chinese!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel - Chinas train system is terrific.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was unexpected and fun.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There was a lot of community at the international dorms, and many chinese students interested in friendship.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: While I welcomed it, and had tried to prepare for it by learning some chinese in advance, the level of english speaking skills outside the university, and even to some extent on campus, was more lacking than I expected.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: So many things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to learn Chinese, embrace local culture, have fun!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Relationships, personal growth, academic advancement.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: So many things going on, it was overwhelming at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
